reviews.review: I really enjoyed everything about this. I only had one minor complaint during one mission where you are finding an identity that leads to a twist and it felt kind of forced to make you ask for help. However; all that aside highly recommend to anyone who enjoys even the tiniest amount of investigation.

The game is extremely immersive and mysterious until the very end. I must say, the ending felt underwhelming, but it leaves space for future projects. There are some plot twists I honestly didn't see coming, which is rare. It's a short game, but it's worth playing!

A fun, short game with a lot of potential for follow-up games. The feel of the game, the computer interface, the live action camera feeds, the interludes are all super well done and immersive. I wish there had been a few more unrelated to the main plot cases just for fun, but otherwise a great game.

Fun detective "FBI" investigative game with its own story within. What a game! Has it's flaws but overall an amazing experience. I'd say it's worth the price for the amount of fun it provides.
 
Well, in this game all you do is type and click, but it didn't get boring at all and nothing really felt repetitive. Some tasks like the chemical analysis and the bomb were really unique, made me wish it wasn't just a one time thing. Even the normal "scan face, look up criminal, send their name" tasks were quite fun. I'm not the sharpest and usually spam the hint button in these type of games, despite this I only asked for help once trying to find a certain badge for a code. The puzzles make you think, but not frustrate you with their complexity.
 
There were two things that I didn't like at all in this game, one being the ending. Even though I did everything right, I still got the bad ending with no satisfying end. The other problem being the big plot twist. As soon as I heard about the COLE family, combined with the files with the 100 names, and the intro cutscene, I basically already knew what the great reveal was going to be. It should've been hidden better, at least until the research facility part of the story.
 
Finally, I do wish there was more build up, that you complete some "filler" tasks before the whole conspiracy story begins. The progression felt a bit too fast for my taste, I would've enjoyed getting a few calls from agents who ask for help, not related to the story. Still this is one of those games where the story hooked me so bad I wished there was a movie of it. Definitely buying the sequal as soon as it's released.

Fun game that stands out in some areas and could have been better in others.

By far the strongest aspect was the sound and music design. I really enjoyed hearing the crescendo kick in right when you discover something interesting. It was well timed, and well executed.

I really enjoyed my time with The Operator, but I finished it feeling like I’d only played the first episode of a much larger game.

The story is genuinely good and kept me engaged the whole way through. Some of the plot twists are fairly predictable, but there are a few moments that genuinely caught me off guard. The problem is that just as things start to really open up… it ends. My first playthrough took around 2 hours, with maybe another hour for a second run to clean up missed achievements.

Where the game really shines is the audio. The music and sound design are fantastic, especially how the soundtrack and effects subtly shift when you uncover something important. Those moments feel great and add a lot of tension. The voice acting across the board is also strong, making the characters feel believable despite the minimal presentation.

Gameplay-wise, I had a lot of fun. There are loads of small, varied “puzzles” that all work in different ways — digging through databases, connecting information, spotting inconsistencies. Nothing ever feels repetitive, but at the same time, many mechanics are introduced, used once, and then never expanded on. It feels like groundwork being laid for systems that never get the chance to evolve.

Overall, this is a great game and absolutely worth picking up on sale to kill a few hours. At its current price point, though, it feels like it’s missing crucial length. The biggest issue is that it feels like the beginning of a story with no ending, rather than a complete experience.

I don’t regret playing it — I just wish there was more of it.

I would classify this as a short narrative game with very light puzzles.

PUZZLES
A majority of the puzzles are signposted and obvious, and they all give a tutorial vibe. The game will teach you how to solve a particular type of puzzle, but then that type of puzzle is never visited again.

There were two puzzles that weren't, but these felt frustrating as:
- the first one had VERY confusing wording and used terms that were not explained ("tickable" being the word I got stuck on)
- the second one you needed to brute force a solution, which is never fun nor rewarding

NARRATIVE
For a mystery game, the final twist was basically shouted at the beginning of the game and I guessed it within the first 5 minutes. All of the cases pertain to the main mystery (no side missions to divert your attention). When you know the secret right away, it's hard to feel motivated to continue playing.

In the end, I felt it was a shallow, predictable, and simple game. It has good bones, but needed a lot more time in the oven

If a sequel does come along, or this team makes a similar game, I hope they:
- Include more puzzles
- Not make the ending obvious
- Playtest all the puzzles to make sure that things are easily understood and enjoyable (without losing the theme)
- Add in some red herrings/busywork 
- Show off their systems! Similar to a Hypnospace Outlaw or The Roottrees are Dead, have us use the mechanics more than once before moving on to a completely different thing. I would have loved to do more searching, scrubbing, etc in the game but didn't have enough opportunities outside each mechanic's single puzzle.

It's probably the best "PC Detective" game I've played. The puzzles make logical sense, the UI is clean, the story is mostly very good, especially in the first half, and the game doesn't hold your hand too much. The game is good at creating a tense, anxious atmosphere, and the blurry first-person scenes are also a really interesting creative choice that I enjoyed.

But it's got some pretty noticeable flaws. While most of the plot twists land successfully, the biggest reveal is very obvious by the time it arrives, and is not as shocking as the game thinks it is. The ending is rushed and unsatisfying. The VO performances range from competent to dreadful, and the script needed an editor to polish the clunky dialogue. And, most egregiously, none of your choices matter, which is always massively disappointing.

Overall, 7/10. If they make a sequel, I'll probably play it.

The Operator brought me a surprisingly deep and immersive narrative experience.
The tension, atmosphere, and decisionmaking felt great, especially in on of the high pressure moments that force you to think rather than act imediately.

I played around 11 hours & loved the experience (2 playthroughs). The story was well writen, emotionally captivating to me, and clearly crafted with meaning behind it.

If there is one area for improvement, it would be adding more branching paths or replayability through alternative storylines.

Overall, this is a well-writen game that I would absoluetly recommend to anyone who enjoys thoughtful, story driven games.
